title: How to Tell If It’s a Cyberattack or Just an Outage
gist: After a cluster of US outages over four business days (Microsoft Exchange, the FAA, JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines and an NSA classified network) amid a US war with Iran, WIRED offers a five-step guide to telling cyberattacks from accidents. Experts stress that about one in a thousand outages is caused by hackers, most big outages are self-inflicted, and attribution often takes days to months.

themes.theme: Clustered US outages, no attack evidence

insights.claim: Over four consecutive business days in mid-November 2026, a mass Microsoft Exchange outage, an FAA technology failure that grounded flights, a JPMorgan Chase software problem, a United Airlines system glitch and NSA classified-network downtime hit US infrastructure, but there is no evidence they were related or caused by hackers.
insights.speaker: Andy Greenberg
insights.so_what: Operational-resilience failures, not hacks, are the near-term risk to watch for these firms; reliability incidents can still carry regulatory and reputational costs.

insights.claim: The apparent multi-bank outage that week appears to have stemmed from inter-institutional transactions involving JPMorgan Chase, showing how one failing node can make many counterparties look down.
insights.speaker: Andy Greenberg
insights.so_what: Concentration risk in payment infrastructure: an outage at a major bank propagates across the system, relevant to systemic-risk and fintech-redundancy theses.

insights.claim: Infoblox's Doug Madory views the clustered outages as a symptom of rising technological complexity and society's total dependence on internet services rather than coordinated attacks, and says such outages will never be fully eliminated.
insights.speaker: Andy Greenberg
insights.so_what: Supports structural demand for observability, resilience and redundancy tooling as complexity keeps rising.
insights.quote: For better or worse, modern society is completely mediated through internet-based services. They have outages from time to time.

insights.claim: Infoblox's head of internet analysis Doug Madory monitors up to a dozen network outages a day and estimates only about one in a thousand is caused by hackers, so the default assumption should be accident absent concrete evidence.
insights.speaker: Andy Greenberg
insights.so_what: Avoid trading on early cyberattack rumors after outages; the base rate strongly favors self-inflicted failures.
insights.quote: One's default position should be that it isn't a cyberattack,

insights.claim: Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince says most current disruptions are standard background noise from complex systems breaking, and IPinfo's João Tomé says most big attack-like outages are self-inflicted by bad updates, configuration changes, cable cuts or power failures.
insights.speaker: Andy Greenberg
insights.so_what: Change-management and configuration errors are the dominant outage driver, favoring vendors of deployment safety and rollback tooling.
insights.quote: Stuff breaks, and that’s just the nature of complex systems.

insights.claim: Outage duration is a clue to cause: faulty updates are usually rolled back in minutes or hours, while ransomware disruptions take days or weeks.
insights.speaker: Andy Greenberg
insights.so_what: A multi-day outage at a listed company raises the probability of a cyber incident and of material financial impact.

insights.claim: Failures at foundational cloud providers such as Amazon Web Services cascade to their customers, so status dashboards from AWS, Google Cloud Platform and Microsoft Azure plus company newsrooms are the first places to check during an outage.
insights.speaker: Andy Greenberg
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler concentration means a single provider's incident can cause broad correlated outages across many companies.
insights.locator: 2. Look at Status Updates From Organizations

insights.claim: Broad network-monitoring sources such as Georgia Tech's IODA, Cloudflare Radar and Watch the Net use the timing, scope and location of disruptions to separate buggy updates, fiber cuts, cyberattacks and government internet shutdowns.
insights.speaker: Andy Greenberg
insights.so_what: Independent network telemetry is a useful real-time signal for event-driven analysis of outages.
insights.locator: 3. Check Trusted Sources of Network Data

insights.claim: Real cyberattacks are often claimed by their perpetrators via ransomware leak sites, ransom notes (as with NotPetya and WannaCry) or hacktivist posts on X and Telegram, but such claims can be exaggerated or false, and some attacks such as the 2016 Mirai attack on Dyn came with no claim at all.
insights.speaker: Andy Greenberg
insights.so_what: Treat hacker claims of responsibility as one data point, not confirmation, when assessing a company's breach exposure.

insights.claim: When neither attacker nor victim confirms an attack, confirmation may come from CISA or private threat-intelligence firms, but it often takes days, weeks or months to reach conclusions.
insights.speaker: Andy Greenberg
insights.so_what: Attribution lags mean markets often price outages before the true cause is known; patience is warranted.
insights.quote: Sometimes you just have to just sit and wait.
